item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J01085","case1_error":"Performs four halving-and-donation rounds instead of the requested two.","case2_error":"Subtracts the overlap from both sprays and never adds it back, excluding germs killed by both from the killed total.","reason":"The first adds extra repetitions; the second removes the shared portion twice when combining overlapping groups.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01086","case1_error":"Uses the third Frank sold, 12 apples, as his remaining apples instead of 24.","case2_error":"Counts four tires per car including spares, omitting the four additional spare tires.","reason":"The first substitutes the removed quantity for the remainder; the second omits an additional component of the total.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01087","case1_error":"Omits the $20 flat fee from the total deposit.","case2_error":"Adds another grown $28 contribution to $120 instead of applying 10% growth to the combined $120 portfolio.","reason":"The first omits a fixed additive charge; the second uses an incorrect growth relation and counts the contribution again.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01088","case1_error":"Uses the first day's total flower count, 50, as its tulip count instead of 30.","case2_error":"Uses the small-light count, 22, as the large-light count instead of 24.","reason":"Both substitute a count belonging to another category into an otherwise correctly evaluated calculation.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J01089","case1_error":"After correct group formulas, introduces unsupported numbers and sums them to 112 without connecting them to those formulas.","case2_error":"Adds the dead chickens to the purchased chickens instead of adding the surviving chickens.","reason":"The first produces an unsupported numerical calculation after correct formulas; the second explicitly writes an incorrect relation for the final population.","judgment":"different"}]}
